note: Ordinance 2024-198, passed on final reading on 2024-10-08 (minutes at https://pasadenatx.gov/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Minutes/_10082024-534), imposed a commercial moratorium on BESS permits. Its preamble, quoted in Ordinance 2025-001, says it would expire 90 days after adoption unless extended after notice and hearing. Ordinance 2025-001 extended it for a 90-day period past January 6, 2025, which ends on 2025-04-06; council passed it on first reading on 2025-01-06 and on second and final reading on 2025-01-07 (minutes 01062025-551 and 01072025-554). Before that end date, council adopted Ordinance 2025-082, adding Chapter 9, Article XII, Energy Storage Systems, to the Code of Ordinances (first reading 2025-03-18, second and final reading 2025-04-01), the regulations the moratorium was meant to give time to draft. Searched for a further extension: council minutes for 2025-01-28, 2025-02-04, 2025-02-13, 2025-02-18, 2025-03-04, 2025-03-18, 2025-04-01, 2025-04-15, 2025-05-06, 2025-05-13, 2025-05-20, 2025-06-17, 2025-07-01 and 2025-11-18 hold no moratorium item after 2025-01-07; the 2025-03-18 and 2025-04-01 minutes mention only Ordinance 2025-082. A full-text scan of all 100 City Council agenda packets posted from 2025-01-06 through 2026-10-20 found the word moratorium only in the 2025-01-06 and 2025-01-07 packets, and no later BESS moratorium item. The AgendaCenter search for moratorium and BESS returned only the January 2025 meetings. Minutes for most meetings after July 2025 and for 2026 are not posted, so the agenda scan is the check for that period. The 2025-10-07 agenda proposes an ordinance adopting the 2024 International Fire Code in Chapter 13 and repealing Ordinance 2025-082, with energy storage requirements moved into it; its adoption was not confirmed. The tracker's October 2026 end date has no support in the city's records. Quoted: "SECTION 2. That the City Council finds it is in the best interest of the City and does hereby extend the commercial moratorium imposed on the issuance of permits for the placement and installation of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) facilities within the jurisdiction of the City of Pasadena, Texas as established by Ordinance 2024-198 for a 90-day period past January 6, 2025." Second reading (agent:blind-reviewer-1 (Claude Code, 2026-10-18), opened): Pasadena imposed a 90-day commercial moratorium on BESS permits on October 8, 2024 (Ordinance 2024-198, under Texas Local Government Code 212). The 400-acre limit NREL compiled sits in Clarke County's zoning code as Section 23.7(11) of Ordinance 39 (passed 2024-09-09): commercial solar fields capped at 400 acres for the whole county, which is a county-wide total rather than the per-lot maximum the record describes. NREL's linked file is the 2025-08-04 JEO draft of Section 23, never adopted in that form, where the same sentence is item 13. The county then replaced its zoning ordinance with Ordinance 42 (amends 31, 33, 34 and 39; public hearing 2025-08-05, adopted 2025-09-17 by Res 25-151, cover says effective September 17, 2025). Section 23.7 of Ordinance 42 and the 2025-09-16 draft both drop the solar clause, and Ordinance 42 has no acreage cap or other commercial solar siting rule; its only utility solar rule is the Osceola Municipal Airport overlay (Section 21, Figure 7), which rates solar power generation equipment not compatible, and so precluded, in Zones A, B and C and subject to additional review in Zones D and E. The county's Ordinances page (modified 2026-09-23) lists #39 as repealed, see #42, and lists no later zoning or solar ordinance (#43 is wastewater). Board minutes and agendas posted 2025-08-04 through the 2026-10-12 minutes (162 files) contain no solar item, and the public hearing notices page lists no solar hearing. The cap therefore stopped applying when Ordinance 42 took effect on 2025-09-17. For the separate open-ended solar moratorium, Res 24-219 (2024-12-16), already in the dataset as queue:q_4083158e5e, no rescission was found in the minutes through 2026-10-12. Quoted: "Zoning Ordinance No. 42 Land Use Regulations Amended Amends Ordinance No. 31, 33, 34, 39 Effective September 17, 2025 ... 28.2 REPEALER/CONFLICTING REGULATIONS All ordinances and resolutions, parts thereof or amendments thereto, in conflict with this Ordinance are hereby repealed. ... Passed, Adopted and Approved by the Board of Supervisors, Clarke County, Iowa, this 17th day of September, 2025." Second reading (agent:blind-reviewer-4 (Claude Code, 2026-10-19), opened): Ordinance 42 (the card's source, opened 2026-10-19) is the county's full restated zoning ordinance, effective September 17, 2025, and states that it amends Ordinance 39. Its Section 23.7 (Other Applicable Standards, items 1 to 11) has no solar item, and a full-text search finds no 400-acre figure, acreage cap or other commercial solar siting rule anywhere in it; the only utility solar rule is the Section 21 airport overlay (Figure 7, Osceola Municipal Airport Zone Chart), which rates Utility Uses (i.e. solar power generation equipment, wind generators, wind farms) NC (not compatible, precluded from development) in Zones A, B and C and AR (additional review) in Zones D and E. To see where the record's value came from I also opened: Ordinance 39 (effective September 9, 2024, https://clarkecounty.iowa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Ordinance-39-Clarke-County-Zoning-2025-Update-Amending-31-33-34.pdf), whose Section 23.7(11) limited commercial solar fields to a max of 400 acres for the entire county; the August 4, 2025 Section 23 draft that NREL cites (https://clarkecounty.iowa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/updated-wind-ordinance-final-003-JEO-Edits.pdf), which still carried that sentence as item 13; the September 16, 2025 Section 23 draft (https://clarkecounty.iowa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Section-23-updated-wind-ordinance-DRAFT.pdf), which drops it; and the September 17, 2025 special meeting minutes (https://clarkecounty.iowa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/9-17-25.pdf), where Res 25-150 waived the third reading and Res 25-151 adopted the Section 23 amendments to Ordinance 42, 3-0. So the 400-acre solar cap applied from 2024-09-09 until Ordinance 42 replaced the text on 2025-09-17, and it does not apply today. The record also misstates its scope: the cap was a countywide total for commercial solar, not a maximum lot size. The county media library lists no later zoning or solar ordinance (the only later ordinances are Ordinance 43 on wastewater and an amended Ordinance 37 on road right of way). This reading does not cover any separate solar moratorium resolution.
